Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and G2436; inexorable:--without mercy.
BiblicalUsage: James warns that judgment without mercy will be shown to the one who has shown no mercy. The word names the pitiless verdict, mercy refused to the merciless.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for judgment without mercy carries no system of its own; its warning is James's, that the mercy we refuse is the mercy we will not receive.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
